title: Model Entry Certification & Documentation Cookbook for New Model Variants
creator: Asha Varma
description: Goal: Create a repeatable 'cookbook' that standardizes how new model variants (and their quantized builds) are certified for inclusion in our model catalog, how version pins are emitted, and how performance profiles are published and documented. The cookbook will contain a metadata template, gating thresholds for perf and quality, a CI checklist for automated validations, and a maintainer signoff workflow. This ticket covers drafting the cookbook, implementing the minimal linting/CI checks, and authoring the catalog docs + quickstart for onboarders.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical metadata template for model entries exists in the model-catalog repo and is referenced by the onboarding docs
Automated metadata lint runs on PRs and fails on missing required fields (format, model_version, quantization flags, runtime_compatibility)
Performance profile publishing flow documented with examples for p50/p95 latency, token throughput, memory footprint, and qualitative eval scores
Clear version pinning guidance and example YAML/CLI commands included; runtime can consume the pin and fall back to compatible variants
A minimal CI job validates published profile artifact (schema + smoke perf harness) in the catalog CI
Handbook quickstart (Confluence) and a short recorded walkthrough are available for the onboarding squad
tasks: Draft metadata template (fields, types, required/optional) and example for 7B/13B/70B variants
Define performance gating thresholds and qualitative checkpoints (e.g., pass if p95<120ms on A100-40GB under 1x batching and gen-lm test set)
Add metadata linter rule and integrate into model-catalog CI
Add schema validation step to catalog publish pipeline
Write the cookbook doc in model-catalog/docs/cookbook.md and Confluence quickstart
Create a template PR that maintainers can use to onboard a new model variant
Run 2 pilot onboardings (one community model and one internal quantized build) and record lessons
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff sync — agreed cookbook scope with PM/Design/Infra. Decided to keep template minimal and extend via labels instead of many optional fields.
2026-02-18: Added draft metric gates (p50/p95/throughput/mem)。 Diego flagged that p95 gating needs to be hardware-normalized — added requirement to record hardware profile in metadata.

2026-02-25: Implemented initial metadata linter rule (PR created). Linter rules: required fields, timestamp formats, semantic versioning for model_version. CI job still flaky on cross-region artifacts — investigating.
2026-03-02: Pilot #1 (community LLM) onboarded using cookbook draft. Found ambiguity around 'compatible_variants' vs 'fallbacks' — clarified language and added example mapping.

2026-03-08: PM review complete. Request from Compliance to add KMS key_id and data_retention_policy fields for private deployment entries — added as optional fields and flagged security_review_required.
2026-03-10: Pilot #2 (quantized 4-bit build) revealed perf profile noise at low token counts. Decided to require a 10k token synthetic warmup in smoke harness to stabilize KV cache effects.
2026-03-12: Draft cookbook merged to model-catalog/docs under draft branch. Next: add CI schema validation and schedule onboarding workshop with Solutions by 2026-03-20.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict gates block community model onboards — Mitigation: allow 'soft-fail' flags and a documented exception process with reviewer signoff
Risk: Perf numbers vary by hardware — Mitigation: require hardware profile and normalized throughput metrics + sample raw runs attached
Risk: Missing fields for private deployments (KMS/audit) — Mitigation: add optional but recommended fields and require security review for any private-scope entries
